RFC9568-5.1.1.3-1.note: TestSendAdvertV3IPv4HeaderTTLProtoDst reads byte 8 of the frame SendAdvert emits and requires 255; single-polarity, buildIPv4Header writes a constant

RFC9568-5.1.1.3-2.note: RA10 re-audit: the check clause is enforced (golden accepts TTL 255; N4 feeds TTL 64 and requires ErrTTL). The 'MUST discard the packet' clause is not: the discard is the return after recordRxError in instance.onPacket (instance.go:669-671), and no tagged unit asserts the FSM sees nothing; removing that return leaves every tagged assertion green (same hole as RFC9568-7.1-6)

RFC9568-5.1.2.3-1.note: TestIntegrationOpenInstanceSocketOptions/v6 reads IPV6_MULTICAST_HOPS back from the tx and NA sockets and requires 255; runs only under integration && linux with CAP_NET_RAW/ADMIN, as the row's marker discloses

RFC9568-5.1.2.3-2.note: RA10 re-audit: the check clause is enforced (v6 golden accepts hop limit 255; TestDecodeV3IPv6ChecksumAndHopLimit feeds 64 and requires ErrTTL). The 'MUST discard the packet' clause is not: no tagged unit asserts that a Decode error keeps the advert from the FSM (the return at instance.go:671), so removing it stays green (same hole as RFC9568-7.1-6)

RFC9568-5.2.2-1.note: RA10 re-audit: TestValidationOrder 3<4 requires ErrType for type 2 and the golden accepts type 1, so the type is checked. The 'MUST be discarded' clause has no assertion: no tagged unit shows a type-2 packet never reaches the FSM (the return at instance.go:671 is untested; same hole as RFC9568-7.1-6)

RFC9568-5.2.4-1.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 re-read after a tag was added to TestEffectivePriorityWithTracking (body unchanged): TestOwnerAutoDetection requires EffectivePriority 255 for the owner configured at 120 and the configured 100 for a non-owner; TestEffectivePriorityWithTracking keeps the owner at 255 under any decrement

RFC9568-5.2.4-2.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 re-read after a tag was added to TestEffectivePriorityWithTracking (body unchanged): TestBoundaryPriority accepts 1 and 254 and rejects 0 and 255 through extractGroupSpecs/validateGroups; TestEffectivePriorityWithTracking floors a tracked decrement at 1

RFC9568-5.2.5-1.note: RA10 re-audit: N5 count-zero requires ErrCountZero on an exact-length count-0 advert and the golden accepts count 2, so the count is checked. The 'MUST be ignored' clause has no assertion: no tagged unit shows the count-0 advert never reaches the FSM (the return at instance.go:671 is untested; same hole as RFC9568-7.1-6)

RFC9568-5.2.6-1.note: TestEncodeGoldenV3IPv4 requires the Reserve nibble 0 on transmission and exact golden bytes; TestDecodeV3ReserveIgnoredOnReceive sets all Reserve bits, re-checksums, and requires acceptance with the interval unchanged

RFC9568-5.2.8-1.note: row quotes Section 7.1 'It MUST verify the VRRP checksum.', which covers both families; the tagged units prove only IPv6 (golden accepts, corrupted v6 checksum -> ErrChecksum). The IPv4 negative exists (TestNegativeReferenceBugs N1b both-sums-fail-rejected) but is not tagged to this row. RA10: for IPv4, Decode dual-accepts the RFC 5798 pseudo-header sum as well as the RFC 9568 Section 5.2.8 message-only sum, so an advert whose RFC 9568 checksum is wrong is accepted when the legacy sum matches (documented interop deviation, docs/features/rfc-status.md RFC 5798 row)

RFC9568-5.2.9-1.note: TestValidateIPv6LinkLocal refuses a global-first IPv6 group and accepts a link-local-first one (transmit side); TestValidationOrder row 13 rejects a received global-first advert with ErrFirstNotLinkLocal

RFC9568-5.2.9-2.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): the cascade confound is removed: the IPv6 group's IPv4 address now follows fe80::1, so the first-address-link-local rule cannot refuse it, and every refusal must carry the family error text ('is not an IPv6 address' / 'is not an IPv4 address'); same-family IPv4 and IPv6 lists validate. Records: revert validateGroup, both polarities.

RFC9568-6.1-1.note: TestAcceptFilterAcceptsNeighborDiscoveryBeforeAnyDrop requires ICMPv6 135 and 136 accept terms ahead of the first drop term in the Accept_Mode False table, and fails if the table has no drop

RFC9568-6.4.2-1.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): Re-read: the unit's body is unchanged; only the 6.4.2 and 6.4.3 Virtual Router MAC proxy tags left it for TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames, so the verdict stands. Prior note: TestInstanceStartupNonOwnerGoesBackup requires a Backup to install no virtual address, the state Ze hands the kernel that answers ARP; TestInstanceOwnerStartupGoesMaster is the Active contrast

RFC9568-6.4.2-10.note: matrix row preempt-lower-priority-no-delay requires no actions (discard); preempt-false-lower-priority re-arms instead, so the discard is bound to Preempt_Mode True

RFC9568-6.4.2-2.note: TestInstanceIPv6VIPLivesOnVirtualMACDevice requires a Backup to install no IPv6 virtual address and the Active router to install it on the vMAC macvlan only

RFC9568-6.4.2-4.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames (QEMU guest, records observed red on backupFilterTables) proves the wire effect: control without the filter forwards a transit datagram sent to the Virtual Router MAC, the vrrp-backup nft prerouting drop stops it. Still weak: the unit calls setBackupFilter by hand, and the product wiring that makes a Backup hold that filter (run sets it at start, doRemoveVIPs sets it before address removal) is proven only by the untagged TestBackupDiscardFollowsTheState; deleting setBackupDiscard from run or doRemoveVIPs leaves every tagged unit green. Owed: tag TestBackupDiscardFollowsTheState for this id, both polarities, with records on run and doRemoveVIPs.

RFC9568-6.4.2-5.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): Re-read: the unit's body is unchanged; only the 6.4.2 and 6.4.3 Virtual Router MAC proxy tags left it for TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames, so the verdict stands. Prior note: TestInstanceStartupNonOwnerGoesBackup requires no virtual address installed in Backup, so the kernel accepts nothing addressed to it; Active contrast installs it

RFC9568-6.4.2-6.note: TestFSMTransitionMatrix backup/shutdown requires exactly StopTimers and a transition to Initialize; the negative is a contrast row (stale timer event keeps Backup)

RFC9568-6.4.2-7.note: RA-FIX re-read 2026-09-27 against the quote re-taken from erratum 7949. TestFSMMasterDownPromotion asserts the promotion emits SendAdvert, InstallVIPs, AnnounceFailover, StartAdvertTimer, EmitStateChange in that order and ends in Master; TestFSMStaleTimerGenerationIgnored binds promotion to the live timer. No tagged unit asserts what the sentence requires of each step: the gratuitous ARP carrying the virtual IPv4 address with target link-layer address the Virtual Router MAC (erratum 7949), the join of the Solicited-Node multicast address, the unsolicited NA with R set, S clear, O set, target the virtual IPv6 address and TLL the Virtual Router MAC, one announcement per associated address, or the Adver_Timer set to Advertisement_Interval (StartAdvertTimer's interval is not read). The frame builders (transport/garp.go buildGARP, transport/na.go BuildNA) carry those fields, but their tests are not tagged on this row.

RFC9568-6.4.2-8.note: matrix row backup/advert/priority-zero requires exactly StartMasterDownTimer with skewDur; equal-priority row arms mdDur instead

RFC9568-6.4.2-9.note: matrix row backup/advert/adopt/equal-priority requires the down timer at mdDur(cfg, 4000), the recomputed interval from the advertised 4000 ms; the discard row emits no action

RFC9568-6.4.3-1.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): TestVRRPNonOwnerMasterAnswersARPWithVirtualMACOnly (QEMU guest, records observed red) proves a non-owner holding the virtual address on the virtual-MAC macvlan answers ARP, and with the address removed no reply is observed. Still weak: the unit installs the address by hand, and no unit tagged for this id shows the product installs the IPv4 virtual address on the virtual-MAC device on promotion (doInstallVIPs through installVIPs); deleting that install keeps every tagged unit green. The sysctl-recipe positive and teardown negative in dataplane_linux_test.go remain proxies. Owed: tag an instance promotion test that asserts the install device and CIDRs for this id.

RFC9568-6.4.3-10.note: matrix row master/advert/priority-zero requires SendAdvert and StartAdvertTimer; a losing non-zero advert sends without re-arming

RFC9568-6.4.3-11.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): TestInstanceIPv6ElectionUsesUnsignedOrder closes both named gaps: the IPv6 operand through the engine (link-local advertisement source) and the unsigned network-byte-order compare (fe80::80 vs fe80::7f, which a signed octet compare inverts). Yield rows assert Adver_Timer cancelled, Active_Adver_Interval set to the advert's 3000ms, Skew_Time and Active_Down_Interval recomputed from it, Active_Down_Timer armed, Backup; the hold row keeps Active, timer armed, 1000ms. With TestInstanceTieBreakComparesTheAdvertisementSource (IPv4). Records: senderWinsTieBreak, observed red.

RFC9568-6.4.3-12.note: losing lower-priority, smaller-ip and equal-ip rows require exactly one SendAdvert and state Active; the winning row demotes instead

RFC9568-6.4.3-2.note: single-polarity; TestInstanceIPv6VIPLivesOnVirtualMACDevice requires the Active router to install the IPv6 address on the vMAC macvlan, which makes the kernel join the Solicited-Node group

RFC9568-6.4.3-5.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames (QEMU guest, records observed red on clearBackupFilter) proves the wire effect: with the filter withdrawn and the address installed the datagram sent to the Virtual Router MAC is forwarded, and while the filter holds it is not. Still weak: the unit withdraws the filter by hand; the promotion wiring (doInstallVIPs calls clearBackupDiscard after the install) is proven only by the untagged TestBackupDiscardFollowsTheState, so deleting that call keeps every tagged unit green while an Active router black-holes the Virtual Router MAC. Owed: tag TestBackupDiscardFollowsTheState for this id, both polarities, with a record on doInstallVIPs (and assert the withdraw follows the install).

RFC9568-6.4.3-6.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): Re-read: the unit's body is unchanged; only the 6.4.2 and 6.4.3 Virtual Router MAC proxy tags left it for TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames, so the verdict stands. Prior note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 re-read after RFC5798 tags were added to TestActiveAddressOwnerAcceptsWhateverAcceptModeSays (body unchanged): owner installs and accepts (instance and acceptfilter tests), Accept_Mode True hands no suppression, and a non-owner with Accept_Mode False gets a suppression: both conditions and the contrast are asserted

RFC9568-6.4.3-7.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 re-read after RFC5798 tags were added to TestActiveAddressOwnerAcceptsWhateverAcceptModeSays (body unchanged): TestActiveNonOwnerWithAcceptModeFalseSuppressesLocalDelivery requires accept=false for exactly the VIP; Accept_Mode True and owner contrasts require accept=true

RFC9568-6.4.3-8.note: matrix row master/shutdown requires StopTimers, SendAdvertZeroPriority, RemoveVIPs, Initialize; TestInstanceShutdownAsMasterSendsPriorityZero proves the executor sends priority 0; backup/shutdown sends none

RFC9568-6.4.3-9.note: matrix row master/advert-timer-expired/matching-gen requires SendAdvert and StartAdvertTimer at 1s; a stale generation sends nothing

RFC9568-7.1-1.note: golden decode accepts version 3; N9 feeds a v2 advert to a v3 group and requires ErrVersion

RFC9568-7.1-12.note: Clause by clause, TestInstanceV3OwnerConflictLoggedAndProcessed (instance.go noteOwnerConflict, called from onPacket). SHOULD verify the local router is not the owner: a v3 owner (IsOwner, Priority 255) receiving a Priority-255 advert records packet.ReasonOwnerConflict, while a v3 non-owner receiving the same advert records nothing, so an owner check that never fires or always fires goes red. Log the event: the owner's first advert writes the owner-conflict log line and the non-owner writes none. Subject to rate-limiting: a second advert 30 s later adds no line and a third 61 s after the first adds one, so an unlimited or never-repeating log goes red. The erratum's correction, keep processing: every owner advert still reaches the FSM as AdvertReceived. MAY indicate via network management: permissive; the counter is asserted at the recordRxError seam only, not on the show/telemetry surface. Discrimination: revert of noteOwnerConflict (positive) and of onPacket (negative) both red. DF-VRRP-5 re-read 2026-09-27: onPacket's only later edit is the syncSourceLocked call after the owner check, which neither counts, logs nor drops, so each clause above keeps its red. RA-VRRP strict re-read 2026-09-27 (independent): agrees enforced. SHOULD verify: owner counts ReasonOwnerConflict on each of three adverts, non-owner counts nothing. Log subject to rate-limiting: log lines 1, 1, 2 at t=0, 30 s, 61 s, non-owner none. Erratum's keep-processing: drainAdvertReceived true for every owner advert. MAY indicate via network management is permissive and binds nothing.

RFC9568-7.1-2.note: golden decode accepts type 1; TestValidationOrder 3<4 requires ErrType for type 2 before the VRID lookup

RFC9568-7.1-3.note: the tagged negative (N2) appends an 8-byte trailer, a packet that still CONTAINS the complete VRRP packet, and is rejected by ze's exact-length rule rather than by this one. A packet missing part of its IPvX address list is the violating input; the truncated case in TestValidationOrder 1<2 is untagged and cuts the fixed header, not the address list

RFC9568-7.1-4.note: RA-FIX re-read 2026-09-27 against the quote re-taken from erratum 8298, which leaves only the VRID check at MUST. Decode (packet/validate.go) returns ErrUnknownVRID when the lookup does not resolve the VRID: TestValidationOrder 4<5 is the negative, TestDecodeGoldenV3IPv4 resolves a configured VRID. The clause 'on the receiving interface' is not asserted: instance.lookup compares the VRID with its own instance, and interface scoping rests on the per-instance socket the transport binds, which no tagged unit exercises. An advert for a VRID configured on another interface is never fed to a tagged unit.

RFC9568-7.1-5.note: Forbidden: accepting an advertisement whose Max Advertise Interval is zero. N6 v3-interval-zero zeroes the 12-bit interval, recomputes the checksum so no other check fires, and fails unless Decode returns ErrIntervalZero. Positive: the golden advert with 100 cs decodes with interval 1000 ms.

RFC9568-7.1-6.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): TestInstanceRxFailedCheckIsDiscarded now covers every mandatory check including the erratum 8301 Max Advertise Interval non zero (v3-interval-zero, reason interval-zero, checksum refilled so only that check fails), plus IPv4 TTL, IPv6 Hop Limit, version, type, fixed fields, addresses, checksum and VRID; each case its own buffer, exact reason, no FSM event, and a control reaching AdvertReceived. Records: revert onPacket, observed red after the new case. The owner check is out of the list under erratum 8298.

RFC9568-7.2-1.note: RA10 re-audit: TestEncodeGoldenV3IPv4 pins the v3/IPv4 checksum to the RFC 5798 pseudo-header form (golden 0xDEFB over src 192.0.2.251/dst 224.0.0.18). RFC 9568 Section 5.2.8: 'For the IPv4 address family, the checksum calculation only includes the VRRP message starting with the Version field and ending after the last IPv4 address'. The test asserts the interop deviation FillChecksum makes (checksum.go), not the RFC 9568 checksum, so the 'Compute the VRRP checksum' clause is asserted contrary to this RFC; the field-fill half is proven only for IPv4 (the IPv6 golden encode is untagged)

RFC9568-7.2-2.note: the tagged unit in packet_test.go asserts only VirtualMAC's derivation (00-00-5E-00-01/02-{VRID}), not that a transmitted frame carries it as source MAC; the wire proof exists in the untagged TestIntegrationAdvertOnPeerVeth (transport_integration_linux_test.go, L2 src == vmac)

RFC9568-7.2-3.note: IPv4 half enforced: TestSendAdvertUsesParentPrimaryV4Source reads the source from the frame and TestSendAdvertNoPrimaryV4SkipsAndCounts refuses to send with no primary. IPv6 half has only the negative TestSendAdvertNoLinkLocalSkipsAndCounts; no tagged unit asserts the IPv6 source is the link-local (the untagged TestIntegrationAdvertV6OnWire does)

RFC9568-7.2-4.note: TestSendAdvertV3IPv4HeaderTTLProtoDst asserts protocol 112 and dst 224.0.0.18 for IPv4 only; the IPv6 next header 112 and ff02::12 destination are asserted only by the untagged TestIntegrationAdvertV6OnWire

RFC9568-8.1.2-1.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): Non-owner half proven: TestVRRPNonOwnerMasterAnswersARPWithVirtualMACOnly (QEMU guest) captures the physical MAC without applyDataplaneSysctls and only the virtual MAC with it (records observed red). Owner half untagged for this id: TestVRRPOwnerAnswersWithVirtualMACOnly and TestOwnerFilterWiredOnPromotionForEveryFamily (ipv4-v3) prove it but carry no RFC9568-8.1.2-1 tag, so deleting the owner filter keeps every unit tagged here green. Owed: RFC9568-8.1.2-1 tags on those two units, both polarities, with records.

RFC9568-8.1.2-2.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): TestEngineWaitsForALateVirtualMACDevice (ipv4) closes the gap: the live macvlanCreator.create runs over a registry that creates the device late and a transport refusing an absent device, and the order is device, install, gratuitous ARP; a device that never appears gives no instance, install or ARP. Deleting waitDevicePresent reddens the positive (records on register.go create, observed red). TestInstanceDelaysAnnounceUntilParentUsable covers the IPv4 address half.

RFC9568-8.2.2-1.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): Both halves proven. Owner: TestOwnerFilterWiredOnPromotionForEveryFamily (ipv6) wiring, records on doInstallVIPs re-recorded after the D-8 edit; TestVRRPOwnerAnswersWithVirtualMACOnly wire effect with a physical-MAC control. Non-owner: TestVRRPNonOwnerMasterAnswersNDWithVirtualMACOnly (QEMU guest) captures a physical-MAC NA with the address on the parent, only the Virtual Router MAC with it on the macvlan under the IPv6 recipe, and no NA once removed; TestInstanceIPv6VIPLivesOnVirtualMACDevice pins the product install device.

RFC9568-8.2.2-4.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): TestEngineWaitsForALateVirtualMACDevice (ipv6): device, install, Neighbor Advertisement order under a late device through the live create, nothing at all when the device never appears; deleting the wait reddens it (records on register.go create, observed red). With TestEngineAnnouncesNothingBeforeTheVirtualMACDevice and TestInstanceDelaysAnnounceUntilParentUsable (address half).
